title: Heating Efficiency vs Outdoor Temperature
dataSources: Mould risk (`mould:risk`), crack meters (`crackmeter:reading`), HVAC filter life (`hvacfilter:life`), structural tilt (`structural:tilt`).
app: Building-health sensors — indoor humidity / mould-risk monitors, crack and tilt meters, HVAC filter-life trackers, and damp sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and ESPHome.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=mould:risk OR sourcetype=ecowitt:obs)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(eval(if(location="living",surface_temp_c,null()))) as indoor, avg(outdoor_temp_c) as outdoor by _time
| eval delta=round(indoor-outdoor,1)
| sort - _time
description: Trends how well your home holds warmth against the outside temperature, a proxy for heating efficiency.
value: A shrinking indoor-outdoor gap for the same heating hints at efficiency loss worth investigating.
implementation: Join indoor and outdoor temperatures in `index=personal`; trend the difference over time.
visualization: Line chart of indoor-outdoor temperature gap.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Building Health & Structural — typical feeds: Mould risk (`mould:risk`), crack meters (`crackmeter:reading`), HVAC filter life (`hvacfilter:life`), structural tilt (`structural:tilt`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `mould:risk`, `ecowitt:obs`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=mould:risk`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Building-health sensors — indoor humidity / mould-risk monitors, crack and tilt meters, HVAC filter-life trackers, and damp sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and ESPHome..

**Author notes:** Join indoor and outdoor temperatures in `index=personal`; trend the difference over time.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "mould:risk", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mould:risk earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Heating Efficiency vs Outdoor Temperature** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=mould:risk`) across the full search range. The `avg` aggregation groups by `_time`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal (sourcetype=mould:risk OR sourcetype=ecowitt:obs)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(eval(if(location="living",surface_temp_c,null()))) as indoor, avg(outdoor_temp_c) as outdoor by _time
| eval delta=round(indoor-outdoor,1)
| sort - _time
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mould:risk earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mould:risk earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.37.9: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Line Chart Of Indoor-Outdoor Temperature Gap (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `mould:risk` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=mould:risk | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
